Brian

I'm trying to insert a line break in the middle of a title on a phylogenetic tree (ggtree) but am having difficulty with using the \n command in conjunction with italics.

and I've also tried:
Atlantic = expression(paste("Atlantic ", italic("M. senile "), "& \n", italic("M. dianthus")))
in order to break this into two lines, but the attached screenshot is what happens.

I would like the title to be:

Atlantic M. senile
& M. dianthus

Thanks in advance!

Heather

messages.subject: Plotting an interaction while controlling for other variables in the model.
messages.subject_clean: Plotting an interaction while controlling for other variables in the model.
messages.body_plain:
(This obviously isn't my research question, but I'm just using it as an illustration.)

Imagine that I'm interested in seeing if there is an interaction between hair colour and weight, as predictors of a person's speed, after accounting for height.

Is the plot that I create below the best (or at least ONE) way of showing this interaction after accounting for height?
Speed = rnorm(1000)
Height = rnorm(1000)
Weight = rnorm(1000)
HairColour = sample(1:3, size = 1000, replace = TRUE)
HairColour <- as.factor(HairColour)
data <- as.data.table(cbind(Speed, Height, Weight, HairColour))

m1 <- lm(Speed ~ Height + Weight*HairColour, data = data)

data$PredictedSpeed <- predict(m1)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Weight, y = PredictedSpeed, col = factor(HairColour), group = HairColour)) + geom_jitter(alpha = .2) + geom_smooth(method = "lm")

messages.subject: Ordering a bar chart using non unique factor labels
messages.subject_clean: Ordering a bar chart using non unique factor labels
messages.body_plain:
Alright so I'm trying to make a 4 paneled bar chart with each showing the top tfidf values and words for it's group. I also want the bars to be in descending order based on the tfidf. I've gotten it to kind of work but some of the values are getting messed up because some of the pages share words in their top 20 and therefore their factors are not unique. I've included the code and chart below. Any way around this?

final_counts  %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(tfidf, .by_group=TRUE) %>%
  mutate(rn = row_number()) %>%
  # mutate(words = factor(words, levels = rev(unique(words)))) %>%
  top_n(20, rn) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  ggplot(aes(tfidf, reorder(words, tfidf), fill=id, alpha=tfidf)) +
  geom_barh(stat = "identity", show.legend=FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Highest tf-idf words in Wikipedia Page",
       y = NULL, x = "tf-idf") +
  theme_tufte(base_family = "Arial", base_size = 13, ticks = FALSE) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.6, 1), guide = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) +
  theme(legend.title=element_blank()) +
  theme(legend.justification=c(1,0), legend.position=c(1,0))+
  facet_wrap(id~., scales="free") +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=2)) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

messages.subject: Re: display of ECDF
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bogdan,

What do you mean by "Equal distance"? In your example, those break points are not uniformly distributed (neither in original form or after log transformed).
For example 0.1 is 10-fold smaller than 1, but the next break, "5", is 5-fold bigger than 1. Do you want these two number to be represent in the x-axis with equally distance from "1"?
My guess is if you can define a function to transform those breaks back into a linear scale, you should be able to use that to transform your data and plot them.

Best,
Kavee
